originality.rationale: The inspected continuous-time fastest-mixing original supplies the general SDP and examples of different graph types but no exact three-class one-pendant-clique phase diagram. The inspected discrete-time lollipop original concerns SLEM subject to stochasticity/stationarity rather than global priced continuous-time rates. Closest earlier network designs use different graph topologies or objectives. Exact unweighted algebraic connectivity or a general optimizer can be consistent with, but does not state or directly imply, the closed-form phases and unrestricted uniqueness. Specialist-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: General spectral-gap SDP techniques make the theorem accessible; further specialist network-optimization literature might already include the same analytical special case.
Some contemporary work on interconnected networks is relevant at the general formulation level but not comprehensively examined for all special graph subclasses.
Novelty is not an independent external-priority certification.

value.rationale: The complete three-phase sharp-support classification solves a natural priced network mixing problem for every core size and all positive cost triples; the second phase deletes internal clique edges, and the costly pendant regime changes even the hub-spoke weight allocation. The unrestricted optimizer uniqueness strengthens merely symmetric-cost design and makes a useful exact benchmark.
